newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq hits new record, enthusiasm seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq hits new record, enthusiasm seen continuing.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite Index jumped 0.44 percent and set a new all-time high Monday as the market built on Friday's gains.

The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 5.72 points to 1316.40, beating the previous record close of 1316.27, which was set on December 9, 1996. The Dow unofficially gained 23 points and set a new record of 6567. The long bond lost 17/32 to yield 6.78 percent.

"There's an influx of new money coming in as corporations add to pension plans and 401(k) plans at the beginning of the year. The money has to go somewhere," said Nelson Gold, a senior vice president of over-the-counter trading at Interstate-Johnson Lane Corp.
"As long as inflation stays down and there are stable interest rates, the market will probably keep going up," another trader said.

Most technology stocks continued to rise after Friday's strong rally, but Apple Computer Inc crumbled after the company said it expected a first quarter operating loss of $100-$150 million. Gainers beat losers 2352 to 1943 on total volume of 603 million shares.
